Subject: Evaluation close pathway, acceptance tests, and exit gates

Hi Maya & Tom,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our mutual action plan discussion, I wanted to put a concise proposal for the close pathway and the concrete acceptance tests NovaCorp will use to sign off the evaluation. The goal: an unambiguous go/no-go by the end of the trial window (week of June 30).

Summary (top-level)
- Success criteria: 1) 95th percentile app latency for the user flow <= 400ms with 2x expected concurrency; 2) average token cost delta vs baseline <= +12%; 3) model output concordance >= 92% on your gold prompt set.
- Exit gates (must pass all): a) SLA smoke test (latency/throughput), b) Security checklist items 1–5 verified, c) Accuracy/concordance above threshold on holdout prompts.
- Acceptance tests: defined smoke scripts (see attached acceptance-test-specs.pdf), automated load test config, and a handoff evidence folder.

Proposed timeline (high level)
- Jun 4–10: Provide final MAP workbook and test artifacts (we’ll attach MAP-v1.xlsx).
- Jun 11–18: Integration + instrumentation (logs, token accounting, tracing).
- Jun 19–25: Run full smoke and load test suite; record results into the acceptance sheet.
- Jun 26–30: Review results, mitigation run if needed, final decision 30th.

Immediate asks for NovaCorp:
1) Confirm the 10 gold prompts we'll use for concordance testing (upload to shared Drive by EOD Jun 5).
2) Confirm if you require additional NDA-level audit evidence beyond SOC-2 artifacts.

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), acceptance-test-specs.pdf (test spec).

I’ll coordinate with Aditya on the instrumentation bits; Lauren will own the decision runbook and signoff doc.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Concordance: the 92% target is fine, but we need to define the scoring rubric (partial credit for semantically equivalent answers). Can you include an example scoring sheet?
2) Latency: does the 400ms target assume cold-starts are excluded? We want to be explicit about warm-only service level.
3) Cost: the +12% token cost delta is acceptable as long as there’s a mitigation path if we exceed it. What does Redwood propose for fallback (quantized model or reduced context) that preserves concordance?

We’ll upload the 10 prompts by EOD Jun 5. Also, Tom flagged procurement: if we get to commit, procurement needs a hardened list of acceptance artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption at rest proof, KMS integration checklist).

Thanks —

Hi team,

Following up with implementation details for the acceptance tests and answers to Maya’s questions. I’ve attached the acceptance-test-specs.pdf in the Drive link but also summarized below.

Scoring rubric for concordance (short):
- Exact match: 1.0
- Equivalent semantic answer (synonym/structure change, preserves factual content): 0.9
- Partial answer (missing minor detail): 0.6
- Incorrect/hallucinatory: 0.0
We’ll run both automatic fuzzy matching and human spot checks on 20% of outputs. Final concordance score = weighted average.

Latency assumptions:
- 400ms 95p target assumes warmed containers and caching enabled (no cold-start samples). We’ll annotate the run to exclude first-request spikes.

Cost mitigation plan (if > +12%):
- Tiered fallback: 1) switch to 8-bit quantized variant for non-critical routes, 2) enable prefix-KV caching for repeated contexts, 3) reduce context window for batched background jobs. We will provide a runbook to toggle these with telemetry checks.

Acceptance test checklist (high level):
- Security: SOC2 summary, KMS key rotation proof, network egress controls verified (docs linked).
- Functional: pass top-10 prompt concordance >=92% across 3 runs; no more than 2 regressions in top-50.
- Performance: 95p latency <=400ms under 2x concurrent user profile; token cost measured across a 48-hour sampling window.

Proposed evidence deliverables to upload to the shared folder by Jun 11:
- Raw load test logs (Gatling export)
- Concordance scoring CSV + human annotation notes
- Instrumentation checklist confirmation

Attachments referenced: acceptance-test-specs.pdf (detailed test cases), MAP-v1.xlsx (milestones & owners).

If NovaCorp needs the scoring rubric formalized into the MAP workbook, I can add a scoring sheet by tomorrow.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer

If you can get the MAP workbook updated with the scoring sheet and the evidence summary by Jun 11, we’ll target the decision on Jun 30 and include the two-week buffer as a contingency in our internal calendar.

I’ll add procurement’s stub PO requirements to the shared folder. Looking forward to the MAP-v1 workbook.
